review_feedback_findings.field: choiceExplanations.Dominant seventh with a flat fifth
review_feedback_findings.quoted_claim: Wrong: that chord has M3–m3–m3, starting with a major third from the root.
review_feedback_findings.issue: M3-m3-m3 gives ordinary dominant7 offsets0,4,7,10. Flattening the fifth gives0,4,6,10, with successive gaps4,2,4 semitones.
review_feedback_findings.correction: A dominant seventh with a flat fifth has a major third above the root, unlike the minor third A-C here.

author_findings.quoted_claim: For an E♭ alto sax, concert pitch is a minor third above the written note (equivalently, a major sixth below).
author_findings.issue: These intervals give the same pitch class but differ by an octave. Alto sax actually sounds a major sixth lower. The question only requests a triad name, so its selected answer remains correct.
author_findings.correction: An alto sax sounds a major sixth below written pitch; at the pitch-class level this is equivalent to adding three semitones.

review_feedback_findings.quoted_claim: Wrong: this would result from transposing only the root correctly and misapplying the interval to other notes.
review_feedback_findings.issue: The correct concert root for written G is B-flat, not E-flat. This does not describe correctly transposing the root.
review_feedback_findings.correction: E-flat is the concert pitch class for written C; written G maps to B-flat.

review_feedback_findings.quoted_claim: Wrong: no consistent transposition interval from G major produces F major.
review_feedback_findings.issue: A consistent major-second downward transposition maps G-B-D to F-A-C. It is a valid transposition, just not the E-flat-alto interval.
review_feedback_findings.correction: F major results from moving G major down a major second, not the major sixth required for alto sax.

review_feedback_findings.quoted_claim: Wrong: this ignores the transposition entirely, as if concert pitch equaled written pitch.
review_feedback_findings.issue: Ignoring transposition would preserve G major, not produce C major.
review_feedback_findings.correction: Leaving the written pitches unchanged would give G major; the required alto transposition instead gives B-flat major.

author_findings.quoted_claim: D, F, A transposes in the wrong direction.
author_findings.issue: D-F-A is not a uniform interval transposition of B-flat-D-F. Pitch-class displacements are4,3,4 semitones, so direction alone does not explain the error; it also changes a major triad to minor.
author_findings.correction: D-F-A changes the interval pattern to a minor triad instead of preserving the major triad under one transposition.

review_feedback_findings.quoted_claim: Wrong: this transposes the melody down a minor third rather than up a perfect fourth.
review_feedback_findings.issue: Down a minor third from B-flat-D-F gives G-B-D, not D-F-A. No uniform pitch-class shift maps the supplied ordered triad to D-F-A.
review_feedback_findings.correction: D-F-A does not apply a single interval to all three notes and changes the major triad to minor.
